title: Lexicographically Smallest String After Applying Operations
summary: Given a string s of even length consisting of digits from 0 to 9, and two integers a and b , you can perform either of the following operations any number of times in any order: - Add a to all digits at odd indices of s (0-indexed).
statement: Given a string s of even length consisting of digits from 0 to 9, and two integers a and b , you can perform either of the following operations any number of times in any order: - Add a to all digits at odd indices of s (0-indexed). If a digit exceeds 9, it wraps around to 0. For example, if s = "3456" and a = 5 , then s becomes "3951". - Rotate s to the right by b positions. For example, if s = "3456" and b = 1 , then s becomes "6345". Your task is to find the lexicographically smallest string that can be obtained by applying these operations. A string a is considered lexicographically smaller than a string b if, at the first position where they differ, the digit in a is smaller than the corresponding digit in b .
constraints: Even-length digit string of length 2–100; 1 <= a <= 9 and 1 <= b < len(s).
Repeatedly add a modulo ten to odd indices or rotate right by b; return the smallest reachable string.
hints: Only finitely many digit strings are reachable, and both operations are reversible within that state space.
Traverse the operation graph while deduplicating states.
From each state generate one addition and one rotation result; enqueue unseen strings and minimize all visited values.
Graph traversal reaches every finite operation sequence, so minimizing visited states yields exactly the smallest reachable string.

tests.explanation: Exploring rotations and odd-index additions reaches 2050, the smallest state.
Rotation makes both original positions eligible for additions; the smallest reachable string is 24.
